    To beginLupin's chocolateCrunchy honeycomb broken into slabs and half dipped in dark chocolateHow to make it150g caster sugar4 tbsp golden syrup2 tsp bicarbonate of soda100g dark chocolate, melted100g milk chocolate, brokenLine a tin with baking paper.Boil the sugar and golden syrup to amber, then whisk in the bicarbonate of soda and pour into the tin.Leave to set, then break into slabs.Dip half the slabs in melted dark chocolate.Serve with the milk chocolate in rough pieces.One-Eyed Witch coconut iceCondensed milk and coconut in white and pink layers, cut chunky, from the Honeydukes jarHow to make itNot on tonight's cookOld-fashioned coconut ice in two layers, snowy white and raspberry pink, set firm, cut into chunky squares and piled into a glass sweet jar.Line a 20cm square tin.Mix 395g sweetened condensed milk with 250g icing sugar, then work in 250g desiccated coconut until stiff.Press half into the tin.Tint the rest pink with a few drops of colouring and 1 tsp raspberry essence, then press on top.Chill for 4 hours until firm, then cut into 3cm squares and pile into a sweet jar.From the hearthLeaky Cauldron stewBow to Buckbeak first. Beef chuck braised 3 hours in dark stock, carrots, crusty breadHow to make it1kg beef chuck, diced2 tbsp vegetable oil2 onions, sliced3 carrots, chopped1 tsp dried thyme775ml beef stock1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce1 loaf of crusty bread50g butterBrown the beef in the vegetable oil in batches.Soften the onions and carrots with the thyme.Return the beef, add the stock and Worcestershire, cover and braise at 160°C.Serve with crusty bread and butter.Knight Bus ham and cheese toastiesHam and gruyère griddled in butter, tomato soup to dunk, a ride with Stan and ErnieHow to make itNot on tonight's cookThick-cut ham and gruyère toasties with mustard, griddled in butter until crisp, with a mug of creamy roast tomato soup for dunking.Roast 1kg halved tomatoes, 1 onion and 4 garlic cloves with oil at 200°C for 30 minutes, then blend with 500ml vegetable stock and 100ml cream and season.Butter one side of 8 slices of thick white bread.Spread 4 unbuttered sides with Dijon and layer 200g sliced ham and 200g grated gruyère, then close.Cook in a pan over medium heat for 4 minutes a side until golden and melted.Serve with the soup in mugs.Sweet thingsMischief managed fudgeVia the Marauder's Map passage to Hogsmeade. Condensed milk fudge squaresHow to make it395g condensed milk150ml milk450g brown sugar115g butterLine a 20cm tin.Melt the condensed milk, milk, sugar and butter together.Boil to 115°C, stirring all the time.Off the heat, beat until thick.Pour into the tin, cool and cut.Tea leaf reading biscuitsSlice and bake Earl Grey and lemon cookies. Trelawney sees the Grim.How to make it2 tsp Earl Grey tea leaves200g butter, softened80g icing sugar1 lemon, zested280g plain flourGrind the tea leaves finely.Beat the butter, icing sugar, lemon zest and tea until creamy, then mix in the flour.Roll into a log and chill.Heat the oven to 160°C. Slice and bake until pale golden.Cool on the tray before eating.Mugs and cupsPumpkin juiceHermione's Time-Turner buys time for seconds. Butternut, apple, honey, ginger, chilledHow to make it400g butternut pumpkin, cubed750ml apple juice1 tbsp honey1/2 tsp ground cinnamon1/4 tsp ground ginger2 cups iceRoast the pumpkin at 200°C until soft and cool.Blend with the juice, honey, cinnamon and ginger until smooth.Strain, chill and serve in glasses over ice.
